description: Docs-family handoff contract (spec / plan review + fix rounds; the docs-family shell + return constants live in template-contract.json#sections). Doc identity is doc_path + doc_hash; write findings, not status — the engine derives status from findings (review) or trusts the declared status (fix). Each property below documents its rule.

phase.description: dispatch phase (review / fix); determined by the engine, not authored.

status.description: The round conclusion (this dispatch's terminal result) — APPROVED: done; CHANGES_REQUESTED: fix the findings (terminal conclusion of a review round; the fix loop runs as its own dispatch); BLOCKED: the round cannot proceed — the failure mechanism lives in failure_category, the reason in blocker. Orthogonal surfaces: failure_category (mechanism channel) and unverifiable[]/plan_conflicts[] (content-level notes) never fold into status. Review may omit this field — the engine derives it from findings; fix (work type) declares it and the engine passes it through. Write findings, not status.

failure_category.description: Failure mechanism channel — which mechanism ended the round (TIMEOUT / CONTRACT_VIOLATION / ENGINE_SELF_WRITTEN / EXECUTION_FAILURE / UNVERIFIABLE / PLAN_CONFLICT). Orthogonal to status (the round conclusion) and to the content-level unverifiable[]/plan_conflicts[] notes. Engine-written on failure paths. A BLOCKED round may satisfy its grounding via this field (see allOf).

doc_path.description: the reviewed document's exact path — must match the doc argument, do not rewrite relative forms.

doc_hash.description: content state token (sha256 of the doc at review time); legacy handoffs may omit it.

findings.description: [{lens, severity, section|file, line?, summary, fix}] — every review finding; severity blocker → CHANGES_REQUESTED, warn/nit → APPROVED (review rolls up; fix keeps declared findings).

file.description: repo-relative path of a file this round changed.

reason.description: why the file changed (finding id / fix intent); omitted entries stay attributed by file.

changes.description: Changed-file attribution ledger (fix rounds declare every file the round touched). Docs rounds carry no commits field — the boundary surface is doc_path; the ledger keeps the same bookkeeping shape as the task family.

cause.description: round-end cause: the failure-category id (EXECUTION_FAILURE / TIMEOUT — the residue-preservation eligibility set) on engine-written death carriers, or the termination sub-cause on legacy salvage records.

exit_code.description: the failed agent's process exit code (1 = run failure, 143 = SIGTERM) — the archived death diagnosis distinguishing exit 1 vs 143; absent on TIMEOUT rounds (the monitor killed the process).

residue_ref.description: Salvaged-WIP stash commit SHA (index-independent: `stash@{N}` indices shift on every push/drop). Written by the residue settlement step on eligible EXECUTION_FAILURE/TIMEOUT rounds with a dirty tree; the re-dispatch resume pre-flight reads it and `git stash apply`s it. Settlement output ≡ resume input.

wip_stat.description: structured WIP scale (files / +M / -M) at salvage time — the recovery carrier's archivable magnitude beside residue_ref; counts brand-new untracked files too.

preserved.description: true when the round's residue was stashed into the recovery carrier (residue_ref + wip_stat present); the settlement step's idempotence flag — an already-preserved carrier never double-stashes.

residue_scope.description: WIP scope summary (`git diff HEAD --shortstat`) — data-driven input for the resume brief appendix.

recovery.description: Residue recovery carrier — engine-written on EXECUTION_FAILURE/TIMEOUT failure rounds: cause + exit_code ride every death (the archived, replayable diagnosis); residue_ref / wip_stat / preserved appear once the settlement step stashed the dirty-tree WIP. Absent on all other rounds. Same law as every structured field: the facts live here, the blocker stays human-readable prose.

artifacts.description: point at files, do not embed report bodies — values are paths (e.g. {"doc": "<path>"}), never inline content.

round.description: review/fix round number (engine-derived; canonical naming embeds it in the filename).

unverifiable.description: Content-level notes — each entry states one claim the round could not verify (what + why: e.g. {claim, why}). A non-empty list makes the round BLOCKED with failure_category UNVERIFIABLE and a blocker summarizing the entries. Dev-measured acceptance items (plan-constraints §口径) are NOT unverifiable: an evidence-contract accepted-noted round records them in `notes`, never writes unverifiable and never blocks.

plan_conflicts.description: Content-level notes — each entry states one plan conflict discovered during the round. A non-empty list makes the round BLOCKED with failure_category PLAN_CONFLICT and a blocker summarizing the entries.

blocker.description: The round's single real blocker line — states what could not be verified and why, or the concrete reason the round cannot proceed. Real sources only (agent-declared / engine gate reason / failure mechanism / unverifiable summary); never fabricated. Omit when nothing blocks (NOT null) — null is invalid. BLOCKED requires a non-empty blocker or a failure_category (see allOf).
